title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Notion
providers.scope_notes: Enterprise for IP restrictions; Business/Enterprise for SAML SSO. Confirm API enforcement and token-expiry requirements with Notion.

controls.name: Limit which connections members can install
controls.what: Restricts members to no restriction, approved & recommended, or approved-only connections.
controls.quote: Approved only: Workspace members can only install connections pre-approved by a workspace owner.

controls.name: Approved connections list (revoke / disconnect)
controls.what: Owners revoke specific users' access to a connection or disconnect all users.
controls.quote: Click the ••• menu to: Filter by user. Revoke specific users' access to a connection. Disconnect all users. Remove the connection from the approved list.

controls.name: Manage page access (connection)
controls.what: Owners choose which pages a connection can access and whether only owners can connect/disconnect it from pages.
controls.setting: Settings > Connections > Manage tab > ••• > Manage page access
controls.quote: Workspace owners on the Enterprise Plan can decide what pages a connection can access, as well as who can connect or disconnect them from pages.

controls.name: Who can add integrations (organization security setting)
controls.what: Org owners enable or disable adding integrations for every workspace, or leave it workspace-managed.
controls.quote: These settings can be Workspace managed so that they can be different for every workspace, Enabled for everyone in your organization, or Disabled for everyone in your organization.

controls_unknown: Whether Notion IP address restrictions apply to internal connection tokens, PATs or public OAuth tokens (help page only describes user sign-in; admin tokens are excluded).
Whether SAML SSO enforcement affects API tokens (not stated).
Whether admins can set a maximum PAT lifetime (creators choose 7 days to 1 year; default 1 year).
Whether internal connection tokens or OAuth tokens expire or can be force-rotated by admins.

authentication.summary: Internal connection tokens, personal access tokens and public-connection OAuth bearer tokens.

federation.details: This path uses a local/static or platform-native credential. Evaluate a separate federation path where listed.

ip_restriction.boundary: Enterprise IP allowlist restricts managed-user sign-in and explicitly does not apply to admin tokens on the admin APIs. Coverage of connection, PAT and OAuth API calls is not documented.

lifetime.summary: Static credential; fixed expiry not verified

renewal.summary: Static token reused for API calls. The Refresh action on the internal connection issues a replacement; no documented expiry.

administration.summary: Connection capabilities plus explicit content access; PATs inherit user access. Admin connection controls and token revocation.
administration.conditions: Enterprise for IP restrictions; Business/Enterprise for SAML SSO. Confirm API enforcement and token-expiry requirements with Notion.

offboard.details: Internal connections run as their own bot user, not tied to a member.

inventory.details: Every Workspace Owner sees all internal connections in the Developer portal; Settings → Connections lists all workspace connections.

token_format.notes: ntn_ for tokens generated since 2024-09-25; older secret_ tokens still valid. Notion says not to regex-validate. GitHub secret types: notion_api_token, notion_integration_token.

log_sources.name: Notion workspace audit log
log_sources.notes: Enterprise only; 365-day retention; UI filter by user/integration/agent; IP included where available. API data-access calls are not listed as events.

log_sources.name: Notion SIEM connection (webhook)
log_sources.notes: Enterprise; real-time JSON webhook of every audit log event; payload field names not documented publicly.

log_sources.name: Developer portal / Settings → Connections
log_sources.notes: Lists internal connections, owners, capabilities and content access; visible to all Workspace Owners.

lifecycle_events.notes: token refreshed; audit log 'Integration secret reset'
new explicit owner can see/refresh token

anomaly_cues: integration.secret_reset or integration.owner_break_glass_added outside a change window
Burst of page.permissions.integration_role_added for one connection, especially on sensitive teamspaces
Connection still active after its creator/owner left the workspace (access persists)
Edits attributed to the connection's bot identity at odd hours or on pages unrelated to its purpose
Token with legacy secret_ prefix still in use (old, never rotated)

containment.steps: Settings → Connections → Develop or manage connections → Refresh the internal connection token (or delete the connection); remove page access; update apps with new token.
containment.notes: Docs say to replace the old token everywhere after Refresh but do not state explicitly that the old token is invalidated immediately. Deleting the connection removes it.

sample_query.query: Event type = 'Integration secret reset' OR 'Integration owner added' OR 'Admin added themselves as integration owner'; Date range = last 90 days
sample_query.purpose: Find who refreshed or took ownership of an internal connection token.

unknown: audit log / SIEM payload field names (actor, IP, user agent)
whether Refresh immediately invalidates the old token
last-used timestamp for internal connection tokens

calls.reveals: the bot user; owner (workspace vs user) and workspace_name
calls.log_notes: Enterprise audit log records integration reads, but whether /users/me specifically logs is not stated

calls.reveals: all pages and data sources shared with the connection
calls.log_notes: Enterprise audit log, 365-day retention; event attributed to the integration/agent actor

calls.reveals: pages in a data source/database, filtered and paginated
calls.log_notes: Page viewed covers an integration/AI tool reading page data; Enterprise audit log, 365-day retention

calls.reveals: full block content of a page (paginated)
calls.log_notes: Reading page data by an integration is captured as Page viewed; Enterprise plan only

unknown: Whether non-Enterprise workspaces log any integration reads (audit log is Enterprise-only)
